utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I just want to pick up from where we left off. I just want to pick up logically from where we left off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Somers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me just one minute, Mr. Cickovic. I'm sorry, but I -- going back to the events of the 16th of April, if we could for a moment, please. You indicated that you were in your apartment when you learned that something had transpired, and that you thought, as a Serb, it would be best to remain in your apartment. Can you please explain that comment? Why, as a Serb, was it more prudent for you to remain in your apartment on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I thought it was best for me to remain in the apartment, because shells were falling all over town and there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that have to do with your being a Serb, that shells were falling all over town? Were your fears based on the shelling or on your ethnic status?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think you need answer that question. If there are shells falling, it is prudent probably, we would take it, to stay inside. Were you worried because you were a Serb, particularly worried because of that, Mr. Cickovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if I were a Croat, I probably would have stayed in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you heard on -- presumably it was the radio, Radio Vitez, an order for mobilisation on the 16th. You waited till the 17th to respond. Was there a particular reason?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it on the radio, but that was later in the afternoon, so that day I didn't think I should go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time in the afternoon did you hear it on the radio?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put it to before supper time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before supper time, probably. In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to register or to sign up, you indicated that you were less than eager to do so, but you were handed a rifle by -- was it Samija? Was that the person who gave you the rifle? And you went.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that I was not eager to go. I said that when I heard on the radio about mobilisation, that I went to the municipality building, or rather in front of the police station, and I asked for a weapon. It's not that Mr. Samija pushed one into my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall find it and read it back in a moment. Can I ask you: When you were on the street and you realised that the call was for all military-aged males, did you not notice an absence on the street of military-aged Muslim males, not necessarily for mobilisation, but simply on the street, on the 17th of April? Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th, when I reported, it is true that there were no Muslims in the streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that raise any concern, or did you think twice about that? Did you ask yourself where were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you find any answers to that question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw the HVO police going to apartments and I saw that a few men had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taken away in what direction? Were they taken away -- excuse me. Were the persons who took them away armed? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the HVO police. They came to my apartment too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the men being taken in vehicles?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw them take them out of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the direction in which they were heading from your building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know any of the persons who were being taken out by the HVO police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name their names, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enes Spahic, Hamed Zukic. That is from my part of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know their families and did their families remain in the building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They remained in the building and after a while they left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask them why their men were taken away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have the time to talk or to ask. I was at the front line. I only had time to go home, take a bath, change, and go back. I did not have much contact with these persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your family remain in your apartment while you were on the front line?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family were, in April 1992, in Trogir, in the Republic of Croatia, as refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you remain, if they left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remained because I thought it was my place to stay in Vitez, and this was just the wife and the children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife, as a Croat, left Vitez for Trogir as a refugee; is that correct? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your three children, are they daughters or sons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two daughters and a son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sending them money? Were you supporting them while they were living away from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your sole means of earning a living at the time, let's say up until May of 1992, the monies you earned from the cafe that your brother Gojko owned? Was that your living?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consult with your brother Gojko before you allowed Mario Cerkez to take your cafe -- his cafe?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no possibility to have contact with Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he not in Glamoc at the time, or had he already gone to Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had already gone. In March 1992 he went to Glamoc, and he spent a very short while there, about a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, you were supporting three daughters and a wife who were refugees. Were they working in Trogir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the sole breadwinner of a family of five, four dependents, and Mario Cerkez was permitted by you voluntarily to take your sole means of earning a living to support other people's families. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was quite well off. I had substantial savings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use those savings to send to your family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I went to visit my family almost every month in Trogir until the conflict broke out, that is to say, until the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Till the 16th of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who ran your cafe while you were away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not necessary because I would go away for two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive from the HVO any proceeds from that cafe? Did you get any monies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the savings or were the savings which you managed to accumulate made from monies that were earned through the cafe?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did your savings come from? From the money you earned in the cafe?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had the cafe, but I worked at the factory, too, and my wife also worked at the factory, that is to say, that we had a pretty big income to live off, and we had substantial savings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the amount of savings you had in the currency at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps about 10 or 15.000 Deutschmark, perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't mention that you served while you were in the HVO under Miroslav Bralo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, did he serve under Miroslav Bralo, that's the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, were you serving under Miroslav Bralo when you first were recruited into the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know two individuals, one who is named Edib Zlotrg and the other is named -- let me see if I can get it correct -- Ermadin Gerina? Do you know those two persons?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know both of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both made comments about your service in the HVO, and I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are asking questions, but we need to have an answer one way or the other. You asked the witness whether you served under Miroslav Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm returning to that point so that the Court can see the buildup. I need the answer as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But the answer was "no." It doesn't seem to be --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. It doesn't seem to be -- yes, it has, it's been missed out on the transcript, but the witness said that he didn't serve under Miroslav Bralo. Now, you want to put to him the two other people who said that he did; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to put to him several facts about his service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Right. On what basis are you going to put this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask him, first of all, he indicated he knew the two individuals who commented, and if perhaps they were wrong in their observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, what is the basis of the comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The basis of the comments, they are statements that were given to the OTP, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have they been disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Certainly Zlotrg was and he testified. Gerina I believe may or -- it may or may not have been disclosed. He was not called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is there anything else that you want to put to him about this matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to first solidly get an answer about his service, and if perhaps there was some gap in his memory; and then I'd like to ask him about the credibility of these two individuals if he knows them well enough to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, but you got some statements. That's the foundation of your, your examination, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The statements and also the testimony, live testimony of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, it is customary when you address a Court to use a customary term, and I'd be grateful if you would do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, that's less important. Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to object to this line of questioning by my colleague Ms. Somers. It is true that Edib Zlotrg was a witness before this Court, but it is also true that in his testimony he did not mention the name of our present-day witness Dragan Cickovic at a single point in time. Also, in the disclosed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. statements by the OTP to the Defence, these persons do not mention Dragan Cickovic. As far as the other person is concerned, mentioned by Ms. Somers, this name was never disclosed, and this person never testified before this Court. So I don't think it would be useful to present to this witness statements that were not handed over to the Defence and that -- and by persons who did not appear as witnesses before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I comment on the disclosure issue, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Ms. Verhaag confirms that the Garina statement was disclosed. It may have been in a very -- two statements were disclosed, the dates I'm not sure of. In March of 1999. And that, of course, the Zlotrg statement was disclosed; and further, the testimony before this Court on the 24th of April, 1999, by Mr. Zlotrg, does make reference to this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll consider the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we come to the conclusion that we're not going to allow this line of cross-examination. First of all, we accept that Mr. Zlotrg did not give the evidence; and secondly, we are not sure it's going to add very much to the case, anyway. We have a large amount of detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That actually then changes, Your Honours, a fair amount of the direction of the cross-examination, because much of it was built on our reading of what was in the transcript on this issue. We made the assumptions that that was why the witness was brought to court, to rebut this particular bit of testimony, so just I'll proceed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I would go elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just let me look.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You can take the matter fairly rapidly, I should have thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Did the Bench wish to have the citation? Would it help just to know what day? It was day 14 of testimony of Mr. Zlotrg. I have page 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We've finished with Mr. Zlotrg. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was no discrimination against the Muslim population and you included comments about no discrimination against the Serb population in Vitez. Are you aware of whether or not the Serb population, tiny as it was, ever tried to assert any identifiable evidence of Serbness, such as raising a flag or having any type of folk custom instituted? Was there any visible aspect to your very tiny population, identifying you as Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know -- and believe me, I don't know a lot as far as this is concerned -- I think there was an SDS in Vitez as well. That is to say that this is a Serb party. That existed in Vitez as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any evidence of the flag of the Republika Srpska or, generally, the old Yugoslav flag that was shown by any members of your community?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of this community. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an individual from Vitez named Miroslav -- I'm sorry -- Mirsad Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- although you do not know the individual, if you accept that he, in fact, lived in Vitez and was a Muslim, there has been evidence given before this Court that this young man was detained and six days after Ahmici had heard from an individual named Vujica. Do you know someone named Vujica who was in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are quite a few Vujicas in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ivica Vujica. He was in charge of military matters for the Jokers at Nadioci. Do you know that gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anyone personally from the Jokers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question I have is about your timing on when you learned about the atrocities at Ahmici. You indicated that it was several days after, through discussion on the streets.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were already in the HVO as of the 17th of April? Were you on the front line, immediately mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The comment that Mr. Ahmic made was that six days --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, we have to try somehow to organise your cross-examination, because you asked this witness whether he knew Mr. Ahmic. He says no. And then I see in the transcript that he doesn't know him. So there must be a follow-up, in a rational reasoning, under which I think we are all functioning, because we have to be told. Either he knew him -- but he told you that he didn't know him, and then you continue making statements yourself. The cross-examination has to be connected to the examination-in-chief. That is the principal function of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I appreciate that. I am trying to -- if, in fact, any of the Vujicas who was known to him, because it is the comment of Vujica that is at issue. It really is not so much Ahmic, other than he as the bearer of the comment. If the Court would like a proffer as to what I was going to ask, I would be happy to give it, to see if -- otherwise I shall move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead, please. You spoke about Mr. Ahmic again, but please go ahead. Ask the witness whether he knows him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge Bennouna. Were you referring to Ahmic or Vujica, Ivica Vujica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vujica. You've dealt with Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Ivica Vujica, do you know an Ivica Vuja? Of all the Vujicas you know, is Ivica Vujica one of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know a couple of Vujica families from Rijeka. There was a friend of mine who was killed in front of the cinema by a shell, a math teacher, his brother. Those are the ones I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in charge of the military affairs for the Jokeri and he was at Nadioci. Do you know that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anyone from the Jokers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We shall move on, then. You commented about Pero Skopljak. What was your relationship with Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any special contact with Pero Skopljak. He came to give political lectures to all the soldiers, not just me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the nature of the political lectures? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what his position was. I don't know much about that. But I know that he spoke about the wounded, the killed, the captured, that the captured musn't be killed, mistreated, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you please to take a look at Z715.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This one is number Z715.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is a document from the 18th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we ask for information whether that was disclosed? It seems it was not, but I would like to be sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I doubt it was. There was no reciprocal discovery issue, so this would be the first time we're presenting it. It is not a new document, but it is not previously disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a Croatian or a B/C/S edition of this document, which is an announcement from HVO Vitez, a public statement, and it is a Pero Skopljak announcement. Can you take a moment, please, just to look at it and see if -- you may have heard it, although you may have been on the front line at that time. Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, let's not have any interruptions for a bit. It doesn't say "Pero Skopljak" on it. I agree. But let us try and move on. This is taking a very long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We shall try to finish it up, since I won't be able to -- [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The comments that I'd like to ask you about that were made by Skopljak were whether or not, in the course of any talks that he gave to you, as a soldier, did he use similar language to what is in the third full paragraph in English -- if it's on the ELMO -- about yesterday -- it's unclear if this actually was done the 17th and came out the 18th, or done on the 17th, referring to the 16th. "Yesterday this became obvious, and we shall provide the public with explicit evidence of how fanatic Mujahedin," et cetera, et cetera, and using terms that essentially highlight aspects of Muslim culture or religion. When he came to the front, did he use language similar to this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The text of this document, would you agree, addresses the rights of the Croat people? Would you agree with that assessment, in your quick reading of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We won't get much further. Have you ever seen this before? Have you ever seen this document before, Mr. Cickovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I shall move on, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, I don't think there's much point putting it to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just help me with this. You say it is a Pero Skopljak document. What is the evidence for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It had come in to the OTP. Unfortunately -- well, if the Court looks simply at the top of the Croatian document, it actually has the facts, point of origin, and for us that is representative of the HVO headquarters and where Skopljak would have been operating at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, it's certainly headed "HVO Vitez." Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About the relationship of Mario Cerkez to the very tiny Serb minority, can you tell us, please: Were any other cafes owned by Serbs in the location -- I'm sorry -- in Vitez? Were there any other Serb-owned cafes or businesses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was one opposite me, a cafe/bar called 072. Probably there were others. But this one was right across the road from mine, 072.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, were those businesses also turned over to the HVO? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The owner of that business, Slobodan Cavic, went to Yugoslavia and left his property to his waiter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was his waiter a Croat, a Serb, or a Muslim; do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he keep the business himself or was it mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The business was run by the waiter, and last year the owner of the cafe/bar sold it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, it was not turned over to the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That business was not turned over to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Z937.2, please. If the usher would also be kind enough, if you have an extra copy, to put the Croatian first page on the ELMO, it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document dated 12th of May, 1993, the signature for which is unfortunately cut off, but it comes from the Central Bosnia command, IZM Vitez, and the top of it indicates a signature by Mario Cerkez with a notation in Croatian, I am told that indicates "great, hooray." Very positive, very happy reception to the news or the contents of the order. This order was handed down while you were in the HVO. Were you aware of the contents of the order that came originally from General Petkovic and appears between him and Radic, Ratko Radic -- I'm sorry, Mladic, Ratko Mladic, indicating that there was a cessation of all hostile activities between the HVO and the Serb army. Did you know about this order? Was it conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just returning for a very brief moment to wind up your cross-examination, I do want to ask you again about your mobilisation because you did say yesterday, and I shall read it, and perhaps you can explain it, it is on -- let's see, of LiveNote it came out on page 101. I don't now how best to reference it for the Chamber. But you were asked about mobilisation, and your answer was, "And so on the 17th of April of that year in the morning, I came to the police building with two or three friends, and there I found the chief of police, Samija, and he told us to report to the 1st Battalion." And then you said, "I would not do it, but he personally gave me the rifle, and I reported to Mr. Bertovic." Why would you not have done it? That is what you said. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I didn't say that I wanted to do it. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask why the mobilisation occurred late in the afternoon or toward dinner on the 16th, inasmuch as you indicated you had learned several days later about events during the early morning at Ahmici on the 16th? Did it raise any questions in your mind about the need for soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was announced on the radio that a conflict had occurred between the army and the HVO, and that all able-bodied men should report in front of the municipality building; and as a man of military age, an able-bodied man, I felt it necessary to report because I was a military conscript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the first time you heard on Radio Vitez or any public means a mobilisation order? Was that the first time when you heard it on the 16th? Did you hear one any other time in April or March, or any other time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it on the 16th on the radio in the afternoon, the 16th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the only time you heard a mobilisation order. I just want to confirm no other incidents of announcements that you did not pay attention to or that did not concern you; this is the first and only order you heard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I think we're just about there. Your injuries, I'd just like to ask you a little bit about the nature of the injuries that you sustained, and I have a few documents, not too many, that you can just confirm. They would be Z1465.9, Z1473.8, 1473.9, and .10, 1473.10. This can be gone through very quickly because they essentially concern the same subject matter. The first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment till we have the documents. It would be helpful, Ms. Somers, if in future they could be got into order before they are handed up to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Surely. Does everyone have them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first one, just to confirm that the nature of your injury, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these can go very quickly, but the first one is 1465.9, and that particular confirmation, which is handwritten in your language, is by Mario Cerkez himself discussing the nature of your injuries. Is that -- is this a correct assessment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, only I wouldn't agree with the dates regarding when I was in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would you correct it to? How would you correct it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the unit from the 16th of April, 1993, it would be correct to say from the 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other documents, 73.10, .9, .8, also address this injury, and without taking the Court's time, the question I wanted to ask you was, from what point did you actually start receiving the monies that were given to you for this disability? When did you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know exactly. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just try and help us with a rough idea. Was it in 1995, or was it more recently?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1995, most probably, but I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive payment for your time as a soldier in the HVO? Did you receive a salary as a HVO soldier while you were serving?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there was no -- you made no money, you made no money, you were living only on savings between 1992 and, let's say, the time of the award of this money?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you consider 50, 60, or 70 German marks to be a salary that soldiers received. Then I did receive that salary, if that can be considered a salary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be a matter for the Judges to consider, but thank you. Excuse me one minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I ask for your indulgence for one minute to make sure I've tidied everything up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One last question. Do you know a woman, a Muslim woman named Edina Hrustic, Hrustic Edina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me something more about her? The surname is familiar, but I can't recall the first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only thing I can tell you about her is a comment that was made by her, I believe to this Chamber, I believe, that she was watching television and heard Miroslav Bralo talk about murderers he committed in Ahmici. That is my association with her. Does that -- would that be your association with her, the comment she might have made? If not, say no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Kuber on the 17th of April, who was holding the defence line there until the troops were mobilised? Who was actually physically on Kuber when you got there, what troops?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I wasn't there. I think there were village guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, yes or no, do you know whether or not Ahmici was in the area of responsibility of your battalion, the 1st Battalion? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is there on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cickovic, you said that late in the afternoon on the 16th of April, a general mobilisation was declared and that you heard it on the radio. Two questions in that connection. Tell us, please, when a general mobilisation was proclaimed, did it apply to all citizens of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the citizens of Vitez was involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this -- when you reported on the 17th in front of the police building, did you see your co-citizens, Muslims, reporting for mobilisation, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When my learned friend from the Prosecution asked you -- when Madam Prosecutor asked you about certain dilemmas that you had to go to the front line, was it because you had no weapon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a weapon or a uniform. I had nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said -- you told Mr. Samija then that you wouldn't go to the front line without a weapon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I also asked for a uniform, but there weren't any available. So I went to the front line in civilian clothes, in sports shoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he gave you a weapon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he gave me a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know now when you reviewed the documents about your injuries and when you said that you weren't in the unit from the 16th but, rather, from the 17th of April, 1993, do you know that all the other citizens who signed up for mobilisation all had this date indicated, the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all had the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regardless of when they reported?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A friend of mine went seven days later. He was afraid of the war, so he joined seven days later, but still the same date is indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. One more question linked to the last question put to you by the Prosecution. Do you know from when the village of Ahmici was part of the area of responsibility of your 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CICKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Cickovic, that concludes your evidence. You are now free to go. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our next witness is the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Our next witness is Mr. Franjo Mlakic. It is extremely short testimony, but I'm not still sure whether he came since we asked the Prosecution yesterday at the end of the day how long they predict for cross-examination of the just finished witness. They told us one hour at least, so we ask the Victims and Witnesses Unit to bring that witness at 10.30, which is just about now. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It looks as though he's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Second thing, perhaps, before the witness takes the oath: We also apologise for not distributing his summary, even though it was entirely finished on Sunday evening, but just by administrative -- our administrative error, it was unfortunately distributed only this morning. I'm having it in my bag for two days. It just happened that we mixed up. But the Prosecution did get their copy, I guess, on the same day when it was produced, so there is -- at least we are not putting them in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Mlakic.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, I shall first ask you to clearly pronounce your name.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I am Franjo Mlakic, nicknamed Pane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were born when?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of February, 1955, in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are married, are you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have to slow down because of the interpretation, because I can see that you are following -- doing it well. We need to have a break between question and answer. So you completed your secondary education and you are an entrepreneur; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you live in Vitez and you've always lived in Vitez, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war in Bosnia, you served with the former Yugoslav People's Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you served it in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not far from Zagreb, in Dugo Selo?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of units were they?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It was a tank unit of sorts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was in 1979, 1980, was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you served the army, with the former army, did you earn any rank?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You enrolled at university studies, natural sciences, in 1974; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many terms did you finish?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Almost two. That is, two semesters, the first year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you have to discontinue your studies?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because I ran into financial troubles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were a good student during that year?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also tried to study at a different faculty at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that too is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that other thing?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It was an institute for the theological culture of laymen at the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also cut that short and went back home?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, do you know a person called Marko Lujic, called Markesa?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that individual very well?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I believe I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Do you remember what was the date of the beginning of the general conflict between the HVO and the BH army around Vitez?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: In the morning hours of the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean 1993?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that date, did the above-mentioned Marko Lujic call you at any time after that and offer you a job?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No sooner did the conflict break out than he did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it that he offered you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: He offered me to be his deputy in the production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cannot recall the exact date, but what do you think -- what do you mean when you say "no sooner did the conflict break out"? So could it have been five, ten days, seven, three?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean some five or six days after the conflict began. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he explain to you what it was about and why was it he who was offering you that job?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because we had already been engaged in similar jobs, and he showed me an order. I believe it was issued by the defence office in the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that document showed what?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: That he had been given powers to set up a team like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from those powers, did it also say that he would be manager or the leader or the shop steward, the man who would be responsible, the man in charge of wartime production?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you the only person whom he gathered into his team or were there other people?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. There were quite a number of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps whose signature figured on that document -- on that order of the defence office?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Marijan Skopljak's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're positive that that document was issued by the municipality authority?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately after that, did you take up the job immediately?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it easy? Was it simple?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Nothing was easy or simple at that time, because there were no production material or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But whatever kind of production, I suppose they needed electricity, they needed energy?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alongside a number of other things?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your supply of electricity regular?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you say that you spent more time with or without electricity?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, we were more without electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when there was no light, what did you do about energy?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We used some generators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But electric power generators need fuel.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: They do, but those were small generators, and then whatever we could switch on to it, say 20 kilowatts, and then we simply adjusted to that, and we also cut down the production according to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell us: What exactly did you manufacture at that time, in those early days, the first couple of weeks, that is, end of April/early May?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Different obstacles, different --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you explain to the Court what did you do?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, in the beginning, you mean. In the beginning. Oh, I see. Well, it was hedgehogs and that kind of hurdles. But as it developed, then the production developed too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned hedgehogs. Will you explain to the Court what that is.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: These are three rods which are put together so that APCs or armoured vehicles cannot get through, something in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you mean to block roads?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during those couple of weeks did you also make some mines or shells?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Not in the early days, but later on, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you explain it to us: The SPS, which covers an area larger than the town, where is it? Where exactly did you try to organise your wartime production?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Down there in the parts where we had mechanical equipment to do that, the place where there were machine tools for mechanical Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. manufacturing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then in August 1993 a different organisation to cover responsibility for wartime production; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which organisation was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We were then put under the defence office of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the person number one in the Travnik defence office?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Anto Puljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that establishment or, rather, Mr. Puljic, did they issue new decisions, new documents to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I got the document for the deputy chief of wartime industry. Mr. Mirko [phoen] was accorded the title of the chief of the military industry, or rather wartime production, as it was called at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, it is Marko, not Mirko, in line 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did it then transpire from those documents that it was wartime production for the Central Bosnian area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name of -- it was clear from the name of the function?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the organisation itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Mlakic, if I understand you well, so you began to do that, to organise the military industry, that is, wartime production, a few days after the conflict broke out. And now the organisation changes, but basically nothing changed for you, because you were at one and the same job all the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, as people would say down there, only bosses changed?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And titles and names changed?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness Mlakic: Are you sure that your chief, Marko Lujic, from the beginning of work for that wartime production and at least until the end of September 1993, was he always there, involved in that activity, and that he had no combat tasks in Vitez units?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I am sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that he did not have any other military tasks?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because he was up there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw him more or less every day or once a week, or how?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Every day we had a meeting, day in and day out, to discuss what had to be done that particular day, so that he was absent very, very seldom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Mlakic, could it be -- was it possible that alongside his job in the factory, your chief, Marko Lujic, was also a gunman or perhaps gun commander, head of the artillery unit or chief for missile systems in the Viteska Brigade, that is, that he had any other role at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, as far as I know, nor did he have any time for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps just for clarity: Later on, as you worked in the factory, you also managed to launch the production of some means of defence, that is, explosive devices. Why did you have to do it in the production, considering all the trouble that you had with getting production materials and the like?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The war production was not organised in that factory alone. It was also organised in other places which made boots and other things. And that factory largely made those weapons which served for the defence. But those were very short-range weapons and they were only distributed around trenches, so that those trenches could put up defence, that is, the front line. No offensive weapons, because we could not do anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you dealt with that domain with some types of weapons -- can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. Something is interrupting here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you worked in that field, in the field of weapons, did you -- could you get some parts for those weapons from elsewhere, from other towns, from other places?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: From the towns which gravitated towards the Lasva region; that is, Vitez, Busovaca, Novi Travnik, what we could control. Not from anywhere further away, since we were fully encircled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And my last question, Mr. Mlakic: You worked there for two years after the war ended in the valley?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because then it was turned over to the Naoruzanje, Vojna Oprema armaments and materiel of Central Bosnia. That was a different institution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is, you kept your job, but there was again a new boss?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you given a different title on this occasion, something -- well, some [indiscernible] Title?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I kept the same title.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you ever issued a formal paper that you were being relieved of this duty?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would mean that you are still at the same job?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are not going there anymore?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. About a year and a half or two after that I stopped and went back to my old business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your colleague, Marko Lujic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, he stayed after me there for a while, for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how long --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know, because I had already -- I was already in business with my own business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he in the factory in 1994?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I also think that he was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he left?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness Mlakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Kordic's defence has no questions for this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, you'll notice that the central questions on the topic of Mlakic were all in leading form. I didn't want to interrupt. It will necessitate my taking the witness through those matters with a little care. The Court will also remember, I hope, that this is the witness I forecast I would be asking matters of that I might have asked of the last witness but one, but would put off for this witness in order to partition matters out. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just confirm, Mr. Mlakic, that your father's name is --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Andrija Mlakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father's name is Andrija?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if you will, what was your involvement in the military affairs of this war? Did you take part in fighting yourself at all?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever claim that you did?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of a Home Guard unit?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or of the Viteska Brigade itself?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever claim that you were a member of either?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're sure about that, are you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the night of the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: 15th of April in the evening, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the day of the 16th of April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: 16th of April, 1993, I climbed a hill above my house that is some 150, 200 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were living in Vitez at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay on that hill for the day of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: On that same hill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for neither of those days -- on neither of those days did you see anything of a man Mlakic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, no. That's the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On neither of those days did you see anything of the man Lujic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because he came to see me, to that hill up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time do you say he came to see you on the hill, and on what day?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but I think sometime between morning and noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which day?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: On the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: About the situation in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us a bit more about this conversation, a little bit more about the hill. The conversation first. What can you remember about it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We talked about how we should start the production, and that he lives right above my house, I told you some hundred metres or so, perhaps 150 as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about how you should start the production. Production of what?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Different means of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just fill in the detail for me. Until the 15th, 16th, you had been doing what?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I was doing all sorts of things. When I say all sorts of things, I was involved in some kind of logistics for military equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not as a soldier at all?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Employed by whom, then?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Nowhere. I was at that time -- I had a private business, too. But I did not work at that time because there was a war going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: And I was going towards Gorazde and bringing something for -- transporting something for Croatia, and there are also papers to show that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you hadn't been specifically involved in armaments production or manufacture at all; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I was purchasing purchases for the production, different production materials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you didn't have any skills in the production of armaments, did you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but there were lads who did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were really, what, a trader? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't a trader. I was purchasing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And selling?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, we were not selling that. It was part -- exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not objection, I would just like to suggest if the Prosecutor will tell to the witness which time they're talking about; otherwise, we will be hearing many, many confusions here. That's my feeling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, I've been asking you about, and I think you understand, the period immediately before the 15th of April, 1993. Do you not understand that to be what I was asking you about?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but could you ask me specifically about, about what there is about what did -- what the documents are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to carry on asking you about what you were doing up and until the time you had this conversation, you see, with the man Lujic. So you were buying or exchanging goods. And how well or otherwise did you know the man Lujic, and in what setting?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because we were both involved in the exchange of this military goods, and he also had equipment for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the business you were involved in something called Vitez Trade?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a business, I think, which had as its other participating members Pero Skopljak, Marijan Skopljak, his nephew; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Along with Dragan Safradin, Zlatko Ruzic, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it would. But Marko and I worked very little through Vitez Trade. They were autonomous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Possibly a last member or another member would be a man called Marijan -- sorry, Damjan Marinic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Marko at the same time had his company called Grom "L".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll adjourn. Earlier you criticised Mr. Kovacic about leading. I've reflected on that. It is not a leading question to ask, "Is Mr. Marko Lujic or was Mr. Marko Lujic head of artillery?" It's not a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Had leading, improper leading questions been asked, he would have been stopped. So any implied criticism is not accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to hear that because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, that's the end of the matter. I'm not going to -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- prolong this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was something else I did want to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it concerns what happened this morning. I was going to raise it in any event. The Chamber criticised Ms. Somers for her lack of use of a form of address to the Court. I have to say that if she did that in any way that was unsatisfactory, she was probably taking the lead from me because perhaps I am not over-generous with my use of forms of address to the Court. I also have to say that her approach to the Court from the first to last has been of scrupulous good manners and politeness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not her good manners which were in question, but counsel should know that if they address the Court, then they should use a proper form of address. It's not a matter which the Court should have to raise; it should be a matter of course. One expects that courtesy at the very least. Yes, we'll adjourn now till half past.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just put one demand before, in order not to interrupt later on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't know about a demand, but you can make a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The point is that the Prosecution is using quite a lot of documents which more or less are not discovered, and we would appreciate if at least the Prosecution, in order not to interrupt during the testimony, if the Prosecution would at least inform us, at that point of time when the document is presented, whether it's a new document, whether it was disclosed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm perfectly happy to do that. I'm not sure whether I'm prepared in relation to all -- the limited number of documents, but I'll do my best with each document as it comes today, and I hope I shan't make any errors about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, just a couple more points. We dealt with your business dealings and you were telling us about the conversation. And I think you said between morning and noon is that correct, on the morning of the 16th, that you went up this hill -- I beg your pardon -- that you had the conversation with Marko Lujic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the occasion when Marko Lujic asked you or called you to be his assistant?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this conversation, when did you first recall the details of this conversation, please, Mr. Mlakic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: This was an informal conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Only later agreement was reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But when were you first asked to be a witness in this case, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Two or three days ago. To be more precise -- well, I can't be very precise, but it wasn't long ago. Two, three days, four days. I don't know exactly. I've been here for I don't know how long. Four days, five days. So it could be about ten days all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to know anything about the content -- I'm not allowed to know and certainly don't want to know anything about the content of what passed between you and the lawyers representing Mr. Cerkez. But just yes or no to this: Did you tell them about this conversation? Did you talk to them about this conversation that you had with Marko Lujic on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did you actually first bring it to mind? When did you first remember it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Maybe -- I could not tell you now for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went up a hill behind Vitez. Is that to the north of Vitez, the east of Vitez, the west of Vitez, or the south?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Towards the southern side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw, as you tell us you did, the man Marko Lujic, was he alone or with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember all these details exactly now. This was quite some time ago. It's been quite a while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the best you can tell us is that it was --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because there was a lot of movement around there, so I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all you can tell us is that it was sometime between the morning and noon?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you certainly can't tell us what the man Marko Lujic was doing at breakfast time, can you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't, can you? You can't tell us what the man Marko Lujic was doing at breakfast time on the 16th of April; you don't know?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not realise, Mr. Mlakic, that you were being brought here to deal with something that was said to have been done and said by the man Marko Lujic on the morning of the 16th of April? Did you not realise that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Well, you were asked about Mr. Lujic's presence, I think, at the factory. You can't account for his presence at the factory one way or another until some days after the outbreak of the fighting, can you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after this conversation that you say you had on the hill was it that you were, in the words of your summary, called to be his assistant?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I could not say exactly now, but about ten days, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you immediately -- did you agree immediately to work for him as his assistant or did you then take a few more days to settle your own business affairs before joining him?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I joined him immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was suggested -- you were asked a question, are you sure that he was always there, and are you sure that he was there all the time. From these days, whenever it was, ten days after the start of the fighting, you weren't in his company all the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't say if he didn't -- while you were busy making munitions, you can't say whether he didn't go off and do other things, can you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: But I don't understand you. What ammunition during which ten days? I mean, I don't understand your question. I did not say the first ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, but even after I got to the factory, you can't say that you're sure he was there all the time because you would be doing your business, and he would have his own different work to do, correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, then, just a few -- just tell us this, please, if you will: You know the area of Vranjica, do you, to the southeast of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Vranjica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were on your hill above Vitez, did you see that area, Vranjica, being shelled or attacked with other weapons?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, not really. It's not that there's this view from that hill towards Vranjica. There is yet another hill there, so I could not get a very good view of Vranjica. These are small hillocks, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness see a -- Your Honour, I'll just check. I think this is a new document in the sense of -- ah. It's not a Zagreb document, if I can use that shorthand, it's new to the Court, and I would forecast that it hasn't been disclosed because it wouldn't have become relevant until -- may not have been disclosed. 1477.8, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us please, I should have asked you this before you looked at the document, what is your understanding of the 92nd DP Viteska unit, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Which unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you'd like now, then, please to look at the document that's before you, if the English could go on the ELMO with the original to the witness. This is a document, Mr. Mlakic, dated December 1996, but it is said to be a document issued at your request because, Franjo Andrija Mlakic is you, and we can see the date of birth given, the 21st of February --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- yes, is you. Now, this document apparently signed by Colonel Dragan Vinac, speaks of your being a member of the 92nd DP Viteska from April 1992 to January 1996. Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It is true that I was wounded, but not near Vranjica but by Krajkovaca. Vranjica is in a completely different area. However, it is not true that I was ever a member of any unit. I asked for this so that I could get -- oh, what do you call it? -- money, money for disability. However, I never managed to get that because those people down there, they didn't want to confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that this document is basically untrue in all its particulars? It's quite detailed. It says you were injured in the stomach area and the left thigh. That's true, is it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm not claiming that that is not correct. I am just saying that I was never a member of the Domobran Regiment or the Viteska, and there are documents for that.
