I asked for this document in order to obtain the rights that disabled persons get, and it's not the same for soldiers and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is it right that it was Krajkovaca that you were injured? Krajkovaca?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says here that you were on the front line of defence. That's untrue, is it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, that is not untrue. It is correct I was at the front line; however, I went there to check the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is going -- was going to check the weapons something that people from the factory did on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, quite, because, because these weapons and ammunitions are made in a very primitive way. Often they wouldn't work, the fuses or whatever. So something like that happened, so I went up there. Something wouldn't fire, so I went to check and to see what it was all about. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, a technician like Marko Lujic would sometimes be required, no doubt, to check on whether a weapon was working or to make sure that it did work when perhaps it had failed. Would that be about right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Here it was a question of ammunition. This was done in a very primitive way, and it wouldn't fire. That was it. It was sort of in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how I can explain this to you technically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you have a look quickly at one more document, 2487, which, again, I think is new but not, I think, Zagreb. It's in the International Armed Conflict binder, I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I gather there may be one page -- I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that there was one page missing in the International Armed Conflict binder. I'm very grateful to the registry for drawing that to our attention. The pages missing from the Court's bundles now I think have been provided; and if they're missing from the Defence bundles, I'm sure they will be provided as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, this document, you see, you say you were never serving in any way, this document purports to be a recommendation that you should have the rank of Captain. That's in 1995. That it sets out under paragraph 3 that you were in the reserve forces from the 16th of April, having joined the armed forces on the 1st of March of 1992. And if we turn over the page on the English -- if the usher would be so good, if you'd like to follow this, if you have the original document before you, and I trust it's legible, I think it is -- it says this: That until March 1992, you gave logistic support for the armed forces of Croatia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It then goes on to say that from March 1992 until the 16th of April, you carried out the same duties, but as a member of the Vitez HVO in the territory of Vitez. Now, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I did not take part in this logistics support as a soldier but as a civilian. It is correct that I went to Gorazde and that I brought in -- how should I put this? -- things that were needed for production, for special purposes, and I obtained that. This document was issued so that ranks could be given in the wartime industry because we in the war industry did not belong to any category of the armed forces. We wanted these people to get something, somehow. What the upshot of all of this is is that we did not get anything. The document was not even recognised by the then Herceg-Bosna, because had they wanted to recognise it, I would have had a rank; I would have not remained what I was and what I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two points that follow from the passage we're looking at, Mr. Mlakic, and your answer. First, it says here quite specifically you were a member -- you were doing your job as logistics for the HVO and as a member of the HVO of the Vitez municipality. Now, just tell us: Is that right? It's not a question of doing it on your own account as a businessman. You were doing it as a member of the HVO, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I carried out these duties as a volunteer, not as a member of the HVO, and not representing any company. I did not take any money for that. I was not paid for that. And I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally on this passage, just look, please, and follow with me what it says. It says: "From the 16th of April until the 1st of August, he was a member of one of the units of the Viteska Brigade using rocket artillery systems."

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Where is this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If it's not there in the original, it's at the foot of the first page, I think you'll find.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Oh, here it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll read it again. "From the 16th of April 1993 until the 1st of August, 1993, he was a member of one of the units of the Viteska Brigade using rocket artillery systems." Now, why on earth, if it wasn't simply true, did you allow such a thing to be recorded against your name, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: For financial support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, are you saying to the Court that it was necessary to claim, falsely, military function in order to get some form of financial support? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because war production did not belong to any one of the branches. That can be seen from all those certificates. And this paper also was not recognised by the then Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Had they recognised this document, I would have been a captain now, and I haven't got a thing now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you see, your explanation, I'm going to suggest to you, Mr. Mlakic, simply can't be correct, because look at the last sentence of the same paragraph. You only give yourself four months or so of military service and then say from the 1st of August, 1993 until today he's been the deputy chief of war production. And that may well have been true. Was that true, that you were the deputy chief of military production, but only from the 1st of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I was that immediately after the outbreak of the conflict, as soon as war production was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man Puljic has given evidence, and I think his account is that you were in that position from the summer. Is the truth that it was from the summer and that until the summer you, and indeed Marko Lujic, were engaged as rocket artillery system operators for the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: That is not true. We were working immediately up there at the SPS, and we immediately established war production, which later moved on to supervision of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this was a situation where the question implied something for which there were no grounds. It is not true that Witness Puljic claimed that. Yes, during his testimony it was mentioned that these persons were in war production before Puljic's office took over war production. This assertion is not correct, and that's not the way it can be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go on with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 9, please. This is what you also allowed to be recorded against your name: First, that you had been supplying illicit weapons to the Croatian population in Central Bosnia; then, in the second sentence, that you had produced vast quantities of military materiel for the defence of Central Bosnia through representatives of Croatian authorities. True or false?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Not through the Croatian authorities. I did all this on my own initiative. I was independent in my activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help us, please, with why, then, in this document, you chose to write down or have someone write down for you that you had been getting quantities of military materiel from the Republic of Croatia and then you actually identify the firms: Pobjeda in Gorazde, Slavko Rodic in Bugojno, Bratstvo in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because I worked with those factories, and I supplied those same factories, in return, with weapons from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these weapons that you were bringing from the Republic of Croatia, can we hear again: Were you trading in them, so that you were acting as a middleman, or were you simply facilitating the movement of Croatian weapons to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I delivered weapons to Foca and Gorazde and Bugojno and Novi Travnik, and I supplied companies with this. And in return I took back certain materiel. This was an exchange of goods, and this can be seen from their documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the -- please answer the question. The weaponry came from the state of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it wasn't a question of your buying it from the state of Croatia in order to sell it and make a profit; it was simply provided by the state of Croatia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that I engaged in exchange. Let me give you an example. I took some weapons to Gorazde, and from them I took some other materiel and drove it to the Republic of Croatia. It's a highly complicated undertaking and one factory cannot do it, so several factories need to be involved. And it was necessary to supply this materiel to various factories and then collect elements in order to put them together, and all the necessary documentation for this exists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the materiel you took back to Croatia? We're going to see one example of the materiel a little later, but tell us what you say you took back.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The materiel that I took was the materiel needed from production, from initial capsules, fuses, and in return I would bring either ready-made weapons or weapons and ammunition that could be made operational in those factories. So I would take to Gorazde the casings, rockets, and things like that. I can't remember exactly, but all the documents are fully in order about that, and I think this Court has those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally paragraph 9 ends in this way in the English. You participated in establishing the first line for production of missiles and shells, that after the conflict you participated actively in the defence of the territory. In the English version that sentence ends in a full stop and then the words "war production" are set out. And then it says during the homeland war on the 6th of November you were wounded at Krajkovaca. Were you wounded at Krajkovaca on the 6th of November as opposed to on the 23rd of July? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I think it was the 23rd of July, but I don't know for sure. But there are the documents, and this can be checked. I think it was in the summer, not as late as this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then the last document -- the very last document on this, just to tidy it up, please, 1226.4. You see -- I'm so sorry. Now, this document, Mr. Mlakic, relates to your work as the deputy chief of the department for war manufacturing, and it says that a resolution was made in the Travnik organisation that the duty of deputy chief should be given to you as of the 1st of October, 1993. Now, the date of this document, if you look at it, at the top, is the 1st of October, 1993, assuming it's an accurate document. So this document, I'm going to suggest to you, cannot have been generated, cannot have been made in 1994 or 1995 in order to get you a pension or in order to get you salary. This is a contemporaneous document and it records the truth, that you were only involved in war manufacturing as deputy chief as of the 1st of October, because until then you had been engaged, as the other documents suggest, in the capacity of a member of the Viteska Brigade using rocket artillery systems. Isn't that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the truth?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then explain how this contemporaneous document of the 1st of October records your engagement as of a date in October 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. Can you explain how this document records your appointment to the job of deputy chief of the department for war manufacturing as of the 1st of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because the first document issued by Marijan Skopljak was a municipal document issued by the municipal department, and this is issued by the Department of Defence in Travnik. So the other was on behalf of the municipality, and this is on behalf of several municipalities, the Travnik department, which covered several municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Skopljak document, do you know where it is?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. Marko just showed it to me, that he has been authorised to form a team for production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Marko Lujic was, of course, a good friend of Mario Cerkez, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not see him in his company?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, we didn't have much time to discuss such things, at least as far as I know. But what I don't know I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is Marko Lujic now?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you because I haven't seen him for two years now because I went back to my old job again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on your account, just so that I've got this quite clear, Lujic did nothing in the course of the conflict that would -- that could cause him shame or embarrassment; he simply manufactured arms. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And we manufactured fortification obstacles, among other things, and also weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sitting on the hill or standing on the hill to the southeast of Vitez when the truck bomb went off?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when that bomb went off?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't with the man Marko Lujic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't help one way or another whether he was involved with that, can you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know with what certainty I could assert that, but he -- I think he was not. I think with certainty he was not. But as far as I'm aware and judging by the way these boys boasted about it, apparently the Vitezovi had done it headed by Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... boasted about it apart from Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: But, but those Vitezovi who were with him, but I don't know them really well because he collected boys from various parts, young men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: And I don't really know him, either, too well. We had quite a number of clashes and disputes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken of these boys. It would help the Chamber to know the names of them. I dare say if you'd like to give the names in private session, that would be allowed to you. Do you know any of the names apart from Kraljevic that you can help us with?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, so far as your own history is concerned, and then I've only got one or -- two other topics, one very brief and one not very long to deal with. Do you know somebody called Selo Mlakic?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Zeljo Mlakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zeljo Mlakic.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I know my brother Zeljo Mlakic, and another -- I know another Zeljo Mlakic. He's also a relative of mine, but I think he died during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at the house of either of those men in October, and particularly on the 20th of October of 1992, and if so, were you throwing a missile or using a missile there on that occasion. Can you remember anything like that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I wasn't firing projectiles, and I don't know that I was in that house, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to deal with the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there something you wanted to add?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not going to deal with the documents that touch on Lujic's own engagement with the Viteska Brigade. They've been dealt with, with another witness, and I don't see any reason to put them to this witness. The Court will remember them. They are 2480.2 and 1009.1, which brings me to the last topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, you understand what's being put to you, that you've given account of working in the production department in the summer of 1993, and it may be that somebody looking at the documents which we've seen might well come to the conclusion that, in fact, you had been part of this unit which was referred to, of the Viteska Brigade, using rocket artillery during that summer, because here are documents which refer to you as a member of the Viteska Brigade, as a member of the unit, and as being in charge of or the deputy for production from the 1st of August or the 1st of October. Now, can you explain to us why these documents can possibly have come into existence if they're not right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because the decision on war production is something that no one wanted to address. There were more than 260 workers involved in war production, and at one point they found themselves in a very difficult position. They had no status, so that more or less all of those people involved in war production sought to have documents of this kind in order to obtain some financial resources and support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who was prepared to forge documents --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who was prepared to forge documents on your behalf in order to give you that status?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The signatory of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's one document that I'm going -- I'm turning now to production of weaponry and so on. There's one document that I've just -- I'm having copied that by oversight hadn't been copied, and can I ask for the registrar's assistance with, I think, an outstanding exhibit which is 1220.2. And it may be necessary for me to try and -- I'm sorry to have not teed this up, set this up. It may be necessary for me to find the original passage in the original version. It's page 11 -- or it's the front page to look at what we're looking at, and then it's page 11 of the text. So first of all what we're looking at comes dated the 28th of September, and it's an assessment to be sent to the Travnik Defence Administration in Vitez, signed by Marijan Skopljak, and it says, "Please find enclosed an assessment of the military, political, economic, and other conditions in the wartime." The next page in English, that is the cover sheet of the document, is headed appropriately "Assessment of Political, Economic, and Other Conditions In Wartime." If we can go to page 11. Then if the usher or the witness likes to hand me the -- sorry, page 11 of the English on the ELMO. Thank you very much. And I'm sure we can find quite easily the parallel page in the B/C/S version. It's the page that lists 600 rockets for multiple rocket launchers. There's only one passage on this document which is available of course for general review by my friends and by the Chamber. That's fine. Absolutely fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see one passage here at the top of the screen in English, and I ask you to find it in the document, it says this: "Wartime production was organised before the conflict with Muslim forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's see if the witness has got it. Have you got that passage?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I've only had the number of pieces here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you bring me the document, I'm sure I'll find it. Probably the usher has found it; he's extremely helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The paragraph that I hope you're looking at reads, "Wartime production was organised before the conflict with Muslim forces. It was organised illegally because of the presence of Muslim personnel in special purpose production." Now, I recognise that on your account, even you weren't there until April, and I'm suggesting to you that you may not have been involved in production until August or October; but from wherever you were there, are you able to interpret this passage for us? And what I'm asking you is this: Does this suggest that there was production before the conflict without the Muslims' knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: In certain segments, yes, but only segments, which means in certain parts that we transported to the republic of Croatia, but these were small and limited quantities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were arming -- you were creating arms and keeping the Muslims ignorant of the fact that you were doing so; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. These were certain parts, parts of weapons. I said a moment ago, to manufacture a rocket is an enormous undertaking and a large number of companies are involved. And if we were preparing just the fuses, then those were the fuses. So this is a hundredth part of a rocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But this was done to the ignorance of the Muslims for how long before the outbreak of the fighting --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: But they participated with us. What do you mean without their knowledge? When I went to Gorazde and took supplies from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you for an interpretation of this passage, if you can help us. "It was organised illegally because of the --"

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, same passage. "It was organised illegally because of the presence of Muslim personnel in special purpose production." Why did it have to be organised illegally because of the presence of Muslim personnel?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this because we were working with Muslims, I, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please, which now is copied is 1166.2. It's a new document, coming right away. It's new, but it's not Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on your account, this was within your period of office. It's dated the 16th of August. And let's look at the subject first. It's a request for the supply of materiels from the Travnik HVO. "Based on the conclusions reached at the meeting of the staff of the office of the HVO vice-president and the presidents of the municipal HVO branches in Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca municipalities regarding procurement of necessary materiel and technical equipment through the HVO coordinating body in Split, we are sending you the specifications of the needed material." And then there's set out bullets, machine-guns, plates, grenades. And it then says this: "After procurement, make materiel available to the logistics department of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, by no means to individual brigades or municipalities." First of all, is that method of requesting or ordering supplies and distributing supplies what happened in the course of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We did make some requests, and little quantities arrived by helicopter and parachute, but this was a drop in the ocean. That was all that could be done. Because our requests were vast, our needs were vast, and that is why we manufactured what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I just want to know if the procedure set out here accords with your recollection of events, and I think it does.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a Puljic document, as we can see. Now --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see that there's a reference of delivering to the office of the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It says, yes, "hand to the office of the vice-president." I think it was Dario Kordic, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that again accord with the general practice at the time so far as munitions requests were concerned?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the standard procedure was. The ammunitions we manufactured we delivered to the logistics centre, and the logistics centre then distributed it among the brigades. And he knew what he had and what they were short of. They did that. There was no need for me to be informed. We just did what was asked of us in view of the circumstances and the materiel we had at our disposal. That is what we manufactured. And what we produced, we delivered to the logistics centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it follow from this document that the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was centrally involved in the ordering and allocation of arms in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I could not tell you that. All I can say is what we produced, what we made, what we gave to whom, and there is the appropriate documentation to show it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one looks at the letter -- the copies of this letter of request, the only identified personnel, apart from the chief of administration and the logistics of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, is the office of the vice-president. I mean, you were dealing with this on a regular basis. Please help us. Was that the person to whom these communications were regularly sent?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. Never was a single such request sent from our war manufacturing unit to this office. The chief of logistics in this area under consideration was Anto Sliskovic, and he was the one to whom everything was delivered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But now you can't explain this document at all and why it was sent there? I had hoped I had given you enough time to look at it carefully.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Very well.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't understand why it went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest, since you make that point, I'm going to suggest you know perfectly well that he was coordinating military matters, and that you also know that you've got to try and deny that in this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, you should not interrupt unless there's a valid reason. Now, why? It's an important question. What is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is very simple. Mr. Kordic was never mentioned during the examination-in-chief. The witness came here to testify about a completely different matter. And now I do not see why this insistence on the document which is self-explanatory. It all says in the document. Now questions are asked of a witness, who has nothing to do with Mr. Kordic, to give his opinion about the document, Mr. Kordic, and I don't know what else, hence the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It is clearly a relevant matter as to the role which Mr. Kordic played -- it's central to this case -- the role, if any, which Mr. Kordic played in military matters. Here we have a request to him, your case being that he was simply a politician, for materiel and equipment. Now, the Prosecution are quite entitled to put the document to a witness, who is a man involved in production, to ask him about it. It's clearly relevant. It's a matter that you will have to deal with in due course. Now, put the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you that you know perfectly well that this request went to him because he was centrally involved in military matters in Central Bosnia, and further, that you're denying that because you know you've got to try and protect him here in Court. Can I have an answer, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I am not familiar with this document. This is the first time I see it. And it has nothing to do with wartime production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look briefly at the next Exhibit, 1426 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, having considered the matter, it's pointed out, and it's probably -- I'm sure it's right, that since you haven't seen the document before, you can have the opportunity to examine the witness after the cross-examination about it. So if you want to cross-examine the witness, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 1246.1. It's a new document. We can look at it briefly, but it's for context and fairness, since this witness has come to talk about, amongst other things, provision of materiels. This document, please, English on the ELMO. Thank you very much. And original for the witness. Would Your Honour just give me one minute while I check something, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in case I've overlooked something that I ought to have dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, dated the 13th of October, comes from Cerkez and deals with on the basis of work to date in the SPS. It's clear that the level of production sometimes slumps and is sometimes stable. And he then goes on to level certain complaints of a detailed nature. It deals with the employment of women. And at paragraph 2 it says this: "We know that sheet metal for the production of anti-personnel directional fragmentation mines is running out, and we warn you to actively engage in finding sheet metal and to maximise production of plastic mines, because Mr. Franjo Mlakic requested two days ago the production of MRUDs begin according to his plan." And he then suggested that such explosive devices had proved to be a guarantee of safety on our lines and must save the municipalities in the Lasva region. Was there generally a successful production of anti-personnel fragmentation mines in your factory?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, were the productions successful, they wouldn't be asking us to make them from plastics, because they killed both from the front and from the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reality is that of course you had high demands for arms, because you were engaged in an armed conflict. But the reality is the factory was successful in turning out a lot of product, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what one can call as successful, because there was all makeshift devices. They were all makeshift. They were not properly adopted devices. That is, made of material that was available on the spot. And we wanted to use it to make something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 1302.2, just touching on the question of helicopters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reality was that you were trading -- not trading -- you were getting arms by helicopter from time to time; correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, some ammunition arrived. Weapons, no. But something was inside, and what fell down, because you know how it is: When something lands with a parachute, some of it was broken. So it did not suffice for a proper battalion, let alone the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the materiel coming in by helicopter was coming in from where? Croatia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was coming in to your factory; correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but the logistic was taking it over from the command, from the military district, and then what was for us, they sent on to us. But a great deal was delivered by parachute, so it landed left and right, that is, both amongst the Muslims and amongst us, if I may call it that, or Muslims and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to respectfully suggest to you, Mr. Mlakic, that if you're engaged in the arms business and you're waiting for supplies, even if you're not responsible for getting the supplies, you're going to know where they came from. Now, where did this stuff come from that came by helicopter? Did it come from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I think that it was run from Grude, but where they did get it from, I cannot really tell you all with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The logical place for it to come from is Croatia; you would accept that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, with some I can agree, with some I can't. It depends on what is made where and how it was done. I told you that it was an extremely complex area. If a particular ball bearing was made down in Mostar, so why should it come from Croatia? You must say specifically what and how, and then I shall be able to give you a definite answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document dated the 3rd of November, signed by Puljic, to the wartime production Marko Lujic, the person under the various HVO precedents, concerns the ordering of a helicopter pad and requires that to be done immediately. And the position is that you had enough -- not trade -- you had enough movement of helicopters by November of 1993 to justify trying to have a proper pad built, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We, I mean, got it up there, but we never managed to make it, because we were short of oil and other things to make this pad, so that the pad and the rest of it was never made.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got nothing else. I'm not going to trouble with other documents. There was one passage in the larger document, 1220.2, that I could have put to the witness. I'll see if he can remember it without going through the exercise in paper. It's again on page 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that in the course of, it must be 1993, there was a time in the production of gunpowder when you were able to supply the Republic of Croatia with 3.000 kilograms of gunpowder?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we almost immediately ran out of electricity. But the quantity was not that. It's just too much, even for that factory, because its annual output was 400 tonnes when it was at its peak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you accept in principle that there's an entry to that effect, if you were providing thousands of kilograms of gunpowder to Croatia, was that for them to convert that gunpowder -- not convert it -- to use that gunpowder in making armaments which were then returned to you, or was it for some other purpose of Croatia? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Sir, a thousand tonnes of gunpowder is a tremendous amount for any type of military plant, let alone Vitez, because it is a big plant, but it cannot make. But they had a warehouse down there. And after the bombing by the JNA -- and it was meant for export to Iraq and other places, and they had their huge warehouses from where they were taking it. But naturally they always got from us because at that time we had this exchange, and at that time we had joint manufacture of weapons and this gunpowder, and it was all shared equally, at least as far as I know, because I did not take a direct part in this distribution. And it would be rather the manager of the Pesit [phoen] who could tell you about that because he was manager at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to settle your understanding, and it may be that there was a misunderstanding, I was speaking about not tonnes but 3.000 kilograms of gunpowder. That was the amount I was asking you about. And are you saying that gunpowder that went to Croatia would be used by them for onward transmission to, was it Iran? Is that what you're saying ? Or Iraq, I think.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I'm referring to the Vitez's warehouse down there. And of the 3 tonnes, I don't know specifically what it is about. If it is while I was up there, the deputy chief, then there is a document about it. And I do not know specifically what 3 tonnes are you referring to. I didn't know which gunpowder. For mortars, for rocket, I don't know. I must know what it's about specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Your Honour, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, on the Exhibit 11662.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mlakic, on behalf of Mr. Kordic's defence, I should like to ask you only a couple of questions in relation to a document that was referred to earlier on. I guess you have this document before you. It is document 1166.2. Will you please just look at the first paragraph. The first paragraph in the original, that is, in Croatian. Based on the conclusions reached at the meeting of the Zagreb office of the deputy president of the HVO and presidents of municipal HVOs of the municipalities in the Lasva; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you understand, do you know who was the vice-president of the civilian government of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The vice-president of the civilian government of the HVO was Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the vice-president who had his seat, his office, in the Lasva Valley, or rather, in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: You mean the government?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know exactly, and I'm afraid -- shall I phrase it differently? I might be wrong, but I think that Mr. Anto Valenta was the deputy prime minister. Was it true or not, I don't know, but I think it is because I'm not a party man. I was never a member of any party, so I wouldn't know those things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, and Mr. Valenta is whom I meant.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: So, one of the employees in Mr. Valenta's office had a meeting with representatives of the authority from these municipalities, but I do not see what this document has to do with wartime production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Will you please answer. I understand. You already explained to the Court that this document had nothing do with wartime production, let's resolve that. But I should like to ask you a couple of questions about this document here. Sir --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, if I can answer, yes, I'm all yours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the first paragraph says that it was a meeting of civilian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, was it something out of the ordinary or perhaps quite ordinary for the civilian authorities of each and every municipality in Central Bosnia, I mean the Lasva Valley in the first place, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busocava, help the military logistically? Was that a regular thing, a common thing? I mean financially, logistically, defence, and whatever.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it is logical because that is what they are engaged in. That is what they are in the municipalities, why a mayor. He's there to look after his municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Anto Puljic, chief of defence of this, of administration of Travnik, was he a civilian?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, you, as somebody who was in the wartime production, you were one of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, if you can put it that way, yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more question, perhaps the last one to do with this document, and the delivery of this document to Mr. Vice-president, as he was the, vice-president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, as this document says. Do you think, was Mr. Kordic a politician or a military man?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a politician.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do not have any more questions, Your Honours, thank you very much for allowing me to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mlakic, just to be on the safe side, my friend asked you about a place called Vranica. Can you see it from the place that you were on the hill above your house on the 16th of April? Will you tell the Court if there -- is there also a locality called Vranjska or Vraniska in the territory of Vitez? Is that how you understood it or --

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. I understood that, that the gentleman was asking me about the mountain called Vranica because there is also a mountain called Vranica, and you cannot see it from our place, and that is the hill that I meant. But where is this Vraniska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. This Vranica, is it to the south?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, you could say it's southeast of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not Vranjska which is below Kruscica, if I can put it that way?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, more to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More to the left. So we're referring to a completely different locality?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you were asked about your exercise of some of your rights, your status rights or your financial rights after the war, and I should like to ask you a couple of questions about this. Would you first explain it to me because there was a term that was used in a document. What did you -- what do you understand by "rocket systems"?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, when you -- when one refers to rocket systems, then it is a set -- a system made of several types of rockets, not only ground rockets but guided missiles, and so and so forth. You know what a rocket system is: Something that can cover a very wide and large area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Mlakic -- or perhaps I am too fast. You must have been familiar with the state of affairs with those weapons, with what I as a layman would call artillery and the like. Now, in those early days of the war in Vitez, or perhaps throughout 1993, was there any weapon which could be categorised as a rocket system?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to look again at a document. I'm referring to your proposal for a rank which you were, which you were about to get; but you never got it, did you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when this document was prepared? Was it you who suggested it be done?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, I was not present there. It was Mr. Marko Puljic who drew up minutes and then took it down to the defence office, but I did not participate in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. Today is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever ask you if you agreed with the content in which all this is listed, your career is listed?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I knew about the document, about the existence of the document, but I never saw it, and nobody ever asked me. The only thing I was asked was whether I would agree to be appointed Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe just for the record, we're referring to document 2487 which was produced before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, the war was over or, rather, was drawing to the end. The wartime production involved how many men, roughly?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: At the outset, about 260 employees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is labour rights began to be settled, and shortly it became quite clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If you will allow me just a little to shorten the story, and please, if the Judges would just give me a sign, I will stop, just to come to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will be very careful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So people began to resolve their labour rights, some regulations were adopted, came out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so it transpired shortly that for you, who are in the wartime production, what did it turn out?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it turned out that we did not participate anyway, that we were nowhere, that the war time production didn't even exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the category, employees in the wartime production.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, people, you say 260 of you, as you tell us, did you feel offended as human beings because you've also invested your sweat and your effort into the defence of the valley, and nobody was recognising your contribution?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that at that time, politically speaking, a solution was being sought for the regulation of the status of all those employed in wartime production?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one -- but only one of the documents relative to that was the document that was shown you before?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but all men from wartime production had such a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So not only you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: All 260 went to all sorts of brigades in order to resolve their status. Not only myself, everybody down to the last one. There isn't a single man who is on the wartime production roster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mlakic, from your point of view, you know what you invested, what you did during the war, and what are the rights that you should enjoy. Is it correct to say that from the ethical point of view, you simply tried to get, by the way of this document, what you believed that you were entitled to in view of what you had invested?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: We didn't do it for ourselves, but for the sake of 260 men who happened to be with us in this wartime production. So it wasn't only that Franjo Mlakic asked for something or Marko Lujic asked something for themselves; we were trying to find a solution for all 260 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that sense, you have no problems with your conscience, with your moral?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you will agree that what it says here about all these valour and all the merits that you have, that it's not correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, no, of course it was a bit done up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think we can move on to another subject. A great deal was said here, but you never were given the opportunity to explain it. The factory, the Slavko Rodic Plant in Gorazde, in Foca and so on, shall I ask you a couple of questions about Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this so that everything is accorded its own time and place. Is it -- all that business that you did regarding all those goods, their destinations and all those localities, did all this happen at a time when cooperation between the BH army and HVO was at its peak and when they both were engaged in the defence against the JNA and the ARS?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And specifically places like Rogoj and Foca and Gorazde at that time were controlled by the BH army, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Foca, not of late; Gorazde was encircled, and I entered -- circled Gorazde three times to deliver them this materiel and cigarettes and whatever else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom in Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: To Pobjeda in Gorazde. That is factory in Gorazde, because I cooperated with the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who had the control, whose side?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you took steps to deliver to the BH army some goods that they needed ten days prior to the outbreak of the conflict. Why did you invest those efforts? What was your motive to give those goods to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we didn't hear the witness. Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Because we had a common enemy, and we thought that jointly we could defend ourselves more successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your motive, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "My patriotism," is the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were familiar with Marko Lujic, he had a son, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his son's name is Mario?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I won't tire you with that. We will need that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are you going to be very much longer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I'm not wrong, perhaps ten minutes or so, maybe fifteen minutes. Surely not more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Surely not. We'll adjourn now. We'll sit again at 25 to 3.00. Mr. Mlakic, would you be back then. Please don't talk to anybody about your evidence during the adjournment until it's over, and that does include members of the Defence team. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.06 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic. Ten minutes, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I hope I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us just finish the subject we started concerning the destinations of the BH army, where you had contacts in terms of weapons supplies. Actually, there was an important institution of the BH army in Visoko, important for Bosnia. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which institution was this?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The logistics base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this logistics base, that was the main logistics base of the BH army for that part of Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there a few times, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you've been going there, did you get to meet an officer named Lemes?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say in two words who he was and why he was there?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: He was the main logistics man, actually in charge of production and armaments, military equipment, for the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a moment to go back to document Z2847, where you were proposed to become an officer. You said at the end that you did not manage to achieve what you had set out to achieve with that document.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not get an officer's rank?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is to say that in the -- or rather, does that mean that as concerns future procedure with these documents, some body did not wish to receive this document?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which body was supposed to decide about this?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know it went to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was within the HR HB?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A document was shown to you here. Let's not waste any time. I'm just going to mention the number, Z1220.2. That is Skopljak's report from the 28th of September, 1993. Did you ever see that document before?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps help Skopljak write this report?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps give him some data through your papers that he cross-referenced then?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to be as brief as possible, we did not go into certain details during the examination-in-chief, and this led to a series of questions from the Prosecutor. Mr. Mlakic, isn't it true that when the defence office, the municipal defence office, started organising war production, that there was a competition in terms of who would be in charge of war production within the SPS? Would it be the municipal government or a higher level of power in the HZ HB? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that competition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, who were some kind of top people in this production, did you understand that one side definitely took over control over this work?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which side was this?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: The defence office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of hierarchy, was it higher or lower than the municipal defence office?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It was higher. It was the department for all of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you mean for the entire region of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that moment onwards, you did not communicate with the municipal authorities any longer, did you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No. No. Not as far as the military part of production is concerned, that is to say, that kind of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. We're only talking about that part. That's the only part that we're interested in. Tell me, please: Do you remember that from that moment onwards, that is to say, from the beginning of August, that at any point in time the people from the municipal defence office asked you for anything?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: They came to ask, but we sent them to logistics for Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those channels of communication, distribution that were envisaged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the mentioned Franjo Sliskovic, the chief of logistics at the level of the Operative Zone, was the main link in that chain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In document Z1246.1, that is the report that you looked at as well. Did you see that MRUD is an abbreviation that was used there? What is an MRUD? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: That is a mine with guided action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are an expert. Is this an offensive or a defensive weapon?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It is a purely defensive weapon, and it is usually put near the operator, and it does not have a long range. Well, it depends from one -- from 50 metres to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, how can a mine be offensive or defensive?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, I'm not a soldier. That is why I asked the witness to explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You asked the question, "you are an expert. Is this an offensive or a defensive weapon?" What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I could ask him to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, no, I'm asking you. You asked, you asked the question. What does the question mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I was perhaps not precise enough. The idea was that some -- what I, as a matter, think offensive weapon, something you can hit somebody, or defensive weapon is something you are trying to protect yourself, like that MRUD. It has no other purpose except to put it in front of your trenches or whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What's an offensive mine?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Something which you fire in another, in another party area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're obviously totally at cross-purposes. I thought a mine was something you put in the ground and somebody stepped on, not something that was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Maybe just one question to clear up this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- because for this one, that's what I understood from the soldiers, what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This MRUD, where is it used specifically?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: In front of trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away from a trench is it placed approximately?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends. 20 to 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it activated from the trench?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is to say that it helps the soldiers who are in the trench to defend themselves if somebody is attacking their trench?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This mine, this kind of mine or this mine, is it used when soldiers are moving ahead, when they are taking a certain area?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: A MRUD cannot be used in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: It is used as an obstacle only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move on to something else. These three tonnes or one tonne of gunpowder were referred to here. I want to ask you more specifically, is it correct or do you know or did you know that in Ploce, and Ploce is a harbour in the republic of Croatia and Central Bosnia, and the SPS primarily used that harbour, is it true there was a permanent warehouse of the SPS there before the war as well?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that warehouse was there because the SPS was a manufacturer of gunpowder and some other products, and they sold these products of theirs in the world market?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these products for the most part were loaded onto ships in Ploce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That warehouse with the goods that were there at that moment happened to be there when the war broke out in Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Ploce yourself? Were you there in the harbour?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I was there but not in the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other warehouses there, like of corn and things like that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Croatia, the fact is that the SPS lost these goods?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact is that Croatia or some Croatian agencies, Croatian authorities took these commodities?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the following: In 1992 and up to a few weeks before the conflict when you exchanged goods, as you said to us, together with the BH army, that the value of the goods that happened to be in Croatia and those warehouses in Ploce, the value was taken into account, and that you were given a counter-value in terms of everything that you had in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you did not know that. Just one more question in relation to this. To the best of your knowledge, all the information that you heard, even rumours from those circles, the people that you met in this connection, when did cooperation stop between the BH army and the HVO in terms of supplies of materiel and the manufacturing of materiel in the war against the JNA?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: I had the last exchange, I can't say now with certainty, but it was certainly about ten days before the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a transaction that you took part in personally?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility of the existence of many other chains and contacts through which this happened?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question [sic] for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether others stopped before you or after you?

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: FRANJO MLAKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mlakic. That concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Our next witness is Mr. Zoran Jukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if you'd like to take a seat. Examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Jukic. On behalf of Mr. Cerkez's defence team, I have several questions for you, and will you please answer them to the best of your recollection. At the same time, please wait with your answer until my question has been translated so that we can facilitate the task of the interpreters. Mr. Jukic, for the record, will you give us your name and your birth?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Jukic. I was born on the 26th of June, 1963, in Vitez, in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're still living in the area -- to be more precise, in the village of Nadioci -- don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married and you are the father of three children?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their ages between 3 and 9?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By occupation you are a radio and television technician?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You graduated from secondary school and specialised in broadcasting equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You served in the former JNA in Nis and Titograd, today Podgorica in Montenegro, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in 1981, and you did not acquire any military rank?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war in Bosnia, you lived in Vitez and you worked in Zenica as a broadcasting technician?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are now a private businessman and you are again providing services in accordance with your qualifications?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, I should like to ask you to look back to the events of the end of 1992 -- to be more precise, December -- when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established. Tell us, please: Did you join in that brigade? If you did, in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: By order, I was appointed, on the 15th of December, as a communications officer attached to the 2nd Battalion, which belonged to Vitez municipality within this brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your duty as a communications expert in Stjepan Tomasevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Mostly it was to train one of the soldiers when our units were going towards the army of Republika Srpska, at that time, Kamenjas, Mravinjac, Slatka voda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that time the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade or, more precisely, the 2nd Battalion that you belonged to, were on the front line against the JNA and the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went to the front line and made sure that the communications among the troops were functioning properly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were wire communications mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequently did you tour the front lines? Did you go frequently?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your commander in the military sense?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: In the military chain of command, my commander was the commander of the 2nd Battalion, Anto Bertovic. And by position, the chief of communication in Stjepan Tomasevic, that is Vladica Babic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Jukic, that in that part of the front line, soldiers took turns between Novi Travnik and Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, only I'm not quite sure where the borderline was between us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the troops would come to the front line, stay there for a while, and after that they would go back to their place of birth and return to their jobs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, as a professional: Where did the communications equipment come from that the brigade used?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It cannot be really called equipment. We were mostly supplied from Slimena, which was a warehouse of the former JNA, so we mainly used those telephones. And they too were in short supply, so then we used regular household telephones and adapted them to our purposes. As for radio transmitters, we didn't have any real ones except two amateur radio stations. We did more harm than good, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your assessment, this communications equipment was of a very poor quality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. One could say it was even worse than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you spent some time there, as a member of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, up until the time the Viteska Brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was in mid-March 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You continued with the same activities, but you were now a member of the Vitez Brigade and not of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I became a signalsman of the 1st Battalion of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your commander remained Anto Bertovic, the same person who was in the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how did you communicate with the local radio amateur club in Vitez? Did you get any equipment from them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, some, but they didn't have too much themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, and we are talking about the second half of March 1993, the main task of the Vitez Brigade was equal to the task of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you continued engaging in the same activities and you visited the front line towards the JNA and the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did this in the month of March, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your visits to the front line, did you go there freely or did you have difficulties going there to inspect the radio equipment or for some other purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I went there sometimes twice a week.
