There were no radio transmitters there, because they couldn't be used, but I went for another reason, most frequently to change the batteries, because the soldiers who came there would take radio transmitters with them and they would take out the batteries from the telephones to use them on the radios.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those were the problems you had in your professional activities, but did you have any difficulties provoked by the BiH army that used to stop you when you went there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then in that case, you would have to compile a report about an incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, something I did on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, I will show you a report dated the 22nd and 23rd of March, 1993, so I should like to ask you to identify it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D96/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, is this a report compiled by you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we see from the contents that it was compiled in connection with your assignment at the position of Slatka voda near Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the dates of the 22nd, 23rd of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that at that time the Vitez Brigade had its men, its shift, at positions near Novi Travnik, facing the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, on the 16th of April, 1993, armed activities escalated in Vitez. Tell me, please, briefly, what you were doing that day, where you were, and what you remember about it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, around 5.30 a.m., I was awakened by a very powerful explosion. So I woke up, I went outside, left my house. As the village is quite densely populated and the other locals had got up too and we were confused. We didn't know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about the village of Nadioci, are you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: And so we got together near the main road. We simply didn't know. We were confused as to what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you. You said you didn't know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time you were a soldier of the Vitez Brigade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't anyone, as a member of the Vitez Brigade, inform you in advance that there would be an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: And since the sound was coming from the direction of Vitez, and we already had those village guards set up, which were some kind of protection of the village, a couple of us went towards a locality called Krc. I was one of them. Some others went in another direction and another group stayed on the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You mentioned the location of Krc. It's a hill overlooking your village, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you climbed on that hill to see what was happening in the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your village of Nadioci, which is in a valley, from that village there is no direct view of the village of Ahmici, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: That is correct. No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But from the Krc hill that you climbed on, Ahmici can be seen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see then in the area of the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: At that point in time we could see houses burning and strong infantry fire could be heard, so we thought that a conflict was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you observed this from a distance of about what, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Roughly two kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did anything happen then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. While we were observing this, we went to a clearing so as to have a better view. We were shot at from the direction of Barin gaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us: This location called Barin gaj, which armed forces had control of that location?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It could only have been the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you went back to your village to take shelter from the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We went back to the village to tell them what was going on, because everyone was disturbed, alarmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: After that we organised ourselves and formed a couple of scouting groups, and so we went to secure the access roads so that should any military attack be launched against us, we could evacuate the village on time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," you mean you as the inhabitants of the village of Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you became a reconnaissance group to report to the village should an attack occur?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is when the so-called village guards were formed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the next few days, those village guards gradually started joining the Vitez Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion, the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You too were a member of the 1st Battalion, 3rd Company, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your direct commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: My immediate commander was the late Captain Slavko Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander of the battalion was Anto Bertovic, as you have said.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you personally do those couple of days after the conflict broke out? What was your assignment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Our assignment mostly was to protect the village if at all possible; if not, then to evacuate it in due course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do that -- what were you personally doing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I was a soldier in one of those observation posts. I can't say trenches because we didn't have them at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to use your professional knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, towards the middle of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, can you describe that in a couple of sentences?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. As we were the most forward line, we had the largest number of attacks, so I used my own private radio station to thwart some of those attacks and to intercept conversations between signalmans of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that position above your village of Nadioci is where you stayed virtually throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the other inhabitants of your village of Nadioci also remain there as the members of the 1st Battalion of the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now going on to point -- a point for which I would request a private session if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, a subject that we touched upon briefly already and that is your attendance at the front line during the Stjepan Tomasevic of March brigade, subsequently Viteska Brigade, and I'm referring to the front on Vlasic. What do you know what was the function of the motel at Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: The function of the motel at Kruscica was to prepare those soldiers who were coming from the front villages to give them some weapons. Well, by and large preparation to tell them what was lying in store for them at that front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that there was a checkpoint at the exit from Kruscica manned by the BH?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was called Fatina Vodica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever have any problems when you would pass with your shift towards Vlasic through the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: The checkpoint which I just mentioned, the Fatina Vodica, is on the opposite side, place, and to face the army of Republicka Srpska, we had to go through Novi Travnik, and the checkpoint was on Kamenjas Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that one was also manned by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that checkpoint did you ever have any problems? Would -- at times did they stop you, take some of your equipment and the like, some of your gear?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also have to write a report on what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes. We were bound to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, I will show you now two such reports, and we'll invite you to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please help us distribute the documents that I already gave the registry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, will you please look at this report dated 26th of January, 1993, and tell us if you are the person signed here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the report shows that on that day, that is, the 26th of January, 1993, you and your driver were stopped by the BH army, and on that occasion your radio equipment was seized and the weapons that the driver had?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it happened near Fatina Vodica at Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the number please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked D97/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now look at the second document which is the report of the next day, that is, the 27th January, and will you please pay attention to item 5, which is page 3 in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this part of the same event in the document 27/2 [sic], or is it perhaps a different incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's the same incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now, tell me, Witness Jukic, if members of the BH army knew that you were going to the defence line against the JNA and the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, they knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yet they seized your weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did they behave? How did they treat you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, they were cursing at us, abusing us verbally, and harassed us generally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they perhaps tell you why they were doing that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours, the previous document was marked 97/2, and it's written in the record 27/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Where have we got to? We've got two documents, one headed "Report For the 26th of January." That apparently is D97/2. I don't think we've got a number for the next one. We'll have a number for it. It's marked "Report."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Next document will be marked D98/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Jukic, to bring this examination to a close, I should like to ask you to help us regarding the technical possibilities for audio surveillance of radio equipment. In lay terms, did the BH army have better equipment or worse equipment than the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I had no means of knowing that, but I can presume that they must have had much better equipment than we -- than the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were quite aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the BH army could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, wait a minute. These are controversial matters, Mr. Mikulicic, and you shouldn't lead. You can ask the witness what he knows about the BH army equipment, and he can tell us, but don't put words into his mouth, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall do so, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Jukic, was, how do you know that the BH army had better, high-grade radio equipment than the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: As somebody who was trained as a broadcasting technician, I went to the Travnik maintenance company, and it was one of the highest ranking in the former Yugoslavia in terms of the equipment they used, so I knew what kind of equipment they had for testing and maintenance, and that part remained under their control in their territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean there it was ABH [sic], in BH's territory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, aware of that fact, and you are saying that the HVO was aware of that. Did HVO soldiers when communicating abide by the rules on confidentiality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: By and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in their communication, did these men and officers of the HVO use their own names or code names?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Code names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is what you know about the subject, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, thank you very much for your answers. I do not have any further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: No questions from Mr. Kordic, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you take the view, Mr. Jukic, that each side was capable of tapping the other's telephone connections; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will presumably allow for the reality that different means of mobile communications existed, including field telephones, that is, I think military telephones, but also ordinary mobile telephones?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I am not aware that there are any ordinary mobile telephones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've had quite a lot of evidence of people speaking of things like Motorolas, but I think they're probably walkie-talkies. Does the reference to something called a Motorola make sense to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, sure. Radio stations, that is amateur radio stations, they were of the Motorola type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the sort of thing that somebody can carry in their hand and walk around with, presumably?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these pieces of equipment were used by some of the senior soldiers, certainly, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Could you rephrase it? When you say senior soldiers, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, people of the level of Blaskic or Cerkez, people like that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't really be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it may be helpful because of the growth of mobile telephones with proprietary names like Motorola, just to make sure that we know what you're speaking with when you speak of a Motorola, what size of equipment are you speaking of, if you could help us? Demonstrate or describe as you prefer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I mentioned Motorola because Motorola made a Motorola product, but I did not see that Motorola. And what you're asking me about Blaskic and Kordic, I am not in a position to know such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter about them for a minute. Just help us about the Motorola. You see, we've had references to Motorolas in the case, and we want to know what it means. Can you describe a Motorola to us?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, a Motorola -- well, perhaps it's the wrong term for it because I do not know what you mean when you refer to Motorola. I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we've had witnesses who have been talking about Motorolas as some form of communication. Do you know what it means, and if you don't, say so. If you know what it means, tell us; if not, we'll ask somebody else.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, a radio station was a Motorola, regardless of whether it was a trademark or other type of radio station, that is what I tried to say. I mean, he called, he called every radio station a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you talk about a radio station, is it something that someone could carry about with them? To us a radio station suggests something which is static, a building or something of this sort.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: That's how we called a radio device, broadcasting device which is smaller and which is portable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Counsel used the expression walkie-talkie. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And would that describe a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It was a pleasure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The short reality so far as, say, the period of time April 1993 and onwards is concerned, is this: Each side could listen to the other, each side did its best to stop the other listening; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no way successfully of blocking completely one's messages from the other side. You did your best, but you couldn't necessarily block everything?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My understanding of your own history is that you were first involved in any brigade only in December 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which case I'm wanting your help very briefly, in view of your experience on this topic, with the development of the communications system in the HVO. Coming as you did from Nadioci, and only joining the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in December 1992, were you aware of any orders that had gone out in the summer of 1992 to use, for example, business organisations, telephone services, for the HVO? Were you aware of that sort of order and that sort of practice?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I did not know about that order, but there was such practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, might I see if this document really needs to be produced, in light of the witness's concession -- not concession; answer. It's not a concession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'll just have a look at this. 190, please. I quite accept that this, Mr. Jukic, is before your time and in a sense not necessarily your immediate area, but if you'd help us with it. It comes from the HVO in August 1992 and is headed "The establishment of telephone communications in Central Bosnia." And in an attempt to contribute to overall defence efforts and in accordance with tasks assigned to ensure the quickest possible elimination of the effects of enemy aggression on the telephone system, and in accordance with existing capacities, the following order is made. I don't think I need trouble to read out 1, 2, 3, or 4, but number 5 says that HVO staffs, business organisations that serves the needs of defence, the municipal leadership and the PT organisation serving the needs of the population shall have priority in receiving telephone numbers. Now, was that practice still in operation when you joined up in December?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then number 6 says that the administrators of the telephone organisations are responsible for allocating telephone numbers, in agreement with the HVO and the municipal leaderships; correct? Was that also in operation at the time that you took over -- or not took over -- you were joined up?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can read, if we need to, ourselves the other provisions, but what it amounted to is that the HVO had effectively taken over, for its priority use, the telephone system; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if you'd help us, please, with another short document, 222, please. It's an existing document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry. There's one here for the ELMO, if it's helpful. And again if the original can go to the witness, and it's page 3 of the English, after we look at the title sheet, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The title sheet makes it clear -- this again predates your joining up. It's the 20th of September and it's Vitez. And it's headed "Tasks of the Central Bosnia Command," and "on the basis of clear need for more expeditious work," and so on. Then if we go straight to page 3 and item 17, we can see that there was the intention then, expressed by Colonel Blaskic, to organise and put into use a full communications centre to find the means of preparing radio packets and obtain and begin operating a fax. Now, there's three that's there, perhaps four. From what you saw when you got there, had this order been put into effect, please?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I was the signalsman in the 1st Battalion, so with regard to this particular paragraph, I had no knowledge of it whatsoever, nor could I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps you can help us with just a couple of bits of it maybe. Does the phrase "full communications centre" mean anything to you from your position within a brigade, or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard quite a lot about packet communications. Can you explain those to us so that we can understand it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It would be hard for me to explain it to you. It would have to be someone who was more knowledgeable about radio packets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you operate a packet system yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I? Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see it operated by others?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right in this? And don't assume I am, because I'm wanting your help. But a packet system does involve the receipt of a piece of paper or something that can be converted into a piece of paper at one end, but it involves something being sent by radio from the other end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to that degree, it's similar to a fax, but it doesn't rely, as perhaps a fax sometimes does, on a land line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't know, just say so. It may be that we need some evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We may need some more on that from somewhere else, I think. Very well. Next exhibit, very shortly, 287.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, you may not be able to help with this, but you're the first person dealing with these matters to come, so that I ask your assistance, if you can give it. You say that you -- it's a document dated the 20th of November of 1992, and it actually comes from Brigadier Petkovic, so it's a very senior document. And it goes to the chief of communications of the HVO Main Staff. But it does deal in the middle of the page with something about packet communications, of which you'd seen, and about security. And it suggests here staff commanders should designate a separate room for working with packet communications, select persons to enter the room, and those persons to be answerable. When you saw packet communications being operated, was it done in terms of a special room with some special security measures associated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period any time from December 1992 to the end of -- well, till April of 1993, I suppose, in light of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, no, I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Again, that will have to await someone else. Were you aware whether the practices in your brigade, broadly speaking, matched the practices in other brigades so far as communication is concerned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't -- I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake. The practices, the level of skills at communication in your brigade, were those broadly similar to the levels of skills and practices in other brigades?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, if I were to tell you -- and there are documents that I can raise if necessary -- that in December of 1992 the Jure Francetic Brigade was having training in radio communications, radio relay communications, and other communications, do you recall whether there had been similar training in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's 382.2. I needn't trouble the witness with it. It's already in as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm going to suggest to you is that a lot of attention was paid to communication. Would you accept that? As one would expect.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that well before the outbreak of the fighting in April 1993, there had been training and so on to achieve as high a level of efficiency as possible. Do you accept that there was some training in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't any training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give any --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there wasn't any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give any explanation for why your brigade may have been less fortunate than others in that respect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, because our brigade at that time practically wasn't even a brigade; it was a brigade on paper only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then again I shan't bother with 342.1, which is another Jure Francetic Brigade document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just give me a minute. Likewise, I shan't bother with 383.1, which is to a similar effect, elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you would be good enough to look at 115.3. This is the last document on this topic. This document comes after the outbreak of fighting and is the 5th of August. And it comes from Travnik, signed by Puljic. But it says this, in connection with a particular degree: "As the regional communications centre of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, which is also in Vitez, has good quality equipment for establishing connections with Mostar ..." Now, you obviously were in Vitez from time to time, at the headquarters. There was good quality equipment there, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I could not have known that. What it says here is probably from a higher level. As member of a battalion, I could not come and see, for example, the regional centre mentioned here of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. I never entered the place, so I have no idea what their equipment was like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may be that at your level you simply don't have, or even claim to have, a knowledge of the overall communications system that was operated by your brigade. Is that the position: You only know about what happened very much at your level, at the soldier's level, and the local command post?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. I knew communications only at the level of communications officer, and that is like a squad leader for signals attached to a battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then I can probably pass over most of the other questions I was going to ask you on this topic. I'll just ask one or two. We've had evidence in this case, you see, of visits to the Busovaca telephone building. You'd have no knowledge of the communications equipment there, would you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. I could not have known about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Hotel Vitez headquarters, did you ever go in there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard suggestions that there were land line connections between Busovaca, and in particular, Mr. Kordic's base, and Vitez. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, then, to your own village. Just a few things about that, please. You started off in 1992 by of course joining the Tomasevic Brigade because that was the only brigade you could join to represent the interests of Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we know, that brigade changed into the Viteska Brigade, effectively. Were you going home every night, or regularly, to Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. My working hours were from 8.00 to 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that we can just have from you a little help with the picture in Nadioci, just a few things. Do you remember an incident in January of 1993 at the house of Ahmed Vehabovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Ahmed what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vehabovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: That is quite unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it may be that there's a mistake in the evidence as it's been recorded. Do you remember the occasion of somebody having a fire at their house, their house being perhaps set on fire in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nadioci is a very small village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you can't really say that. Nadioci is a medium-sized village, consisting of two parts. That's what it's called: Lower Nadioci and Upper Nadioci. I'm in Lower Nadioci, by the Zenica-Travnik main road, or rather my house is by that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then of course in February there was the murder at Nadioci by the man Bralo, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that Bralo may have been detained for a short period of time, but he was allowed out afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I know that he had been detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But only for a short period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know when he was released. I believe he was released for the conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who he was released by?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: How could I know? I don't know. How could I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the village of Nadioci, was there a man by the name of -- maybe many men by the name of Delic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: There are quite a few families in our village with the surname of Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'll be permitted, if I may forecast -- I can't guarantee, but you'll be permitted to go into private session if any of these questions require you to seek that. But you say you heard something about what happened at Ahmici. Did you hear anything associated with the man Delic from your village, or one of the men Delic from your village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were down on the road, so you saw the activity of the Jokers, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify that question for me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was hoping you would be able to help us. But you saw the Jokers come and go to the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were soldiers in the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What soldiers were they? Ordinary Viteska Brigade soldiers or someone else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. They were not members of the Viteska Brigade. It was some other unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when were you first aware of their being there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps ten or fifteen days before the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many, if you could estimate their number?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of fighting, there was no question of any build-up of Mujahedin in your village, was there? It's not reported anywhere. No question of that happening?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was there the development of people from -- is it Varazdin? Do you know the place called Varazdin, if I'm pronouncing it even remotely correctly, in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, before the fighting, of the arrival of men in black uniforms from that part of Croatia into your territory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No. No one from there ever came to the area that I lived in. No one from that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By April of 1993 you were in what grouping? It's my mistake for having missed your evidence in detail. You're now in the Viteska Brigade, and in what part of it? What battalion? What company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: A member of the 1st Battalion of the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that your commander was Slavko Papic, I think.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the late Slavko Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been any change in company commanders between the 1st Company and the 3rd Company or had Slavko Papic always been commander of the 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Slavko was commander of the 3rd Company until he was killed during a BH army attack against Kratine, against our position there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The companies were formed where, in Vitez? By which I mean where did they meet when they were called for duty?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you had to report for duty, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: When? Could you explain, please? Could you tell me which duty?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went for duty sometime in March of 1993, maybe you went to different places. Just tell us: How were you called for duty? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I really did not understand what you are referring to. In which period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: March 1993, if you had to report for duty, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of task?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you had to go to the front line, if had you to go to the front line. You say that you went for duty to the front line. Did you report anywhere first or did you go straight up to the front line? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, as a member of the 1st Battalion, at that time when we went towards the army of Republika Srpska, I reported for work every day, and that is when I was given tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where did you report?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: At the command of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the command of the 1st Battalion was where?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: At the Workers' Education Centre in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to complete this topic, this part of this topic, the other battalions' headquarters -- or commands, rather, the other headquarters' commands were also in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that the companies were formed in Vitez. They weren't formed on a local, geographical basis, were they?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It is my opinion that companies were formed just as you had put it in that other question, at certain locations. So we, Nadioci, are the last towards Busocava, so that was the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you best would like to help me, please, with a document, Exhibit 653. If you could have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that's being produced, I'm confident that I can finish within 10 minutes, if that would help. Can I also add: I'm also confident, if there's only the one witness that there is for tomorrow, though I have yet to see the witness's summary, that evidence will not take very long, I don't think. But it may well be, if the Chamber is enthusiastic for this, that some or all of Friday's work could be brought forward, but that's for later consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, I think let's deal with that now. I think we should do that. Immediately we finish with the witness tomorrow, we should go on to the motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. I mean, obviously we may not be immediately as prepared for everything that we might have been, but we will, of course, do everything we can to be absolutely up to date by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Perhaps it will be helpful if we said we'll start -- it seems convenient to start with the Defence motions, three Defence motions, which could be taken together. There are then various administrative matters, which I mentioned on Monday, about exhibits. I can't remember exactly what they are. And then there's a motion which the Prosecution have filed recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There are two motions, actually. There was the one that was referred to on Monday and another one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment, just one moment. The Chamber would wish if possible to finish the matter tomorrow, deal with everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I rather thought that might be the case. We'll do what we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just, please, look at this document. You see, this is a document dated the 14th of April, and it relates to the Viteska Brigade, and it says that it relates to the 1st Battalion, and it then says, "Lists of personnel from the 1st Battalion positioned in the villages." Now, when we look at the 3rd Company, which you say you were a member of, it was headed by Ivica Drmic; when we look at the 1st Company we see its commander was Slavko Papic. You feel quite sure that it was the 3rd Company of which you were a member, or may there be some scope for error?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: There is an error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it also records as to the 1st Company under Slavko Papic, which may or may not relate to you, that there were 20 soldiers positioned in Nadioci. Can you help us with that, please? You see, it doesn't say "coming from," it doesn't say "living in"; it appears to say "positioned in."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, the reference is to the inhabitants of the village who at any point in time can become soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can understand that, that's why I asked you whether the companies were simply formed in Vitez, or whether they were in any way geographically based. And you seem to be accepting that they were simply formed in Vitez so that there would be no particular need for all -- any company's soldiers to come from, it might be five different villages. Is the position that, is the position that there were soldiers on the 14th of April ready for action in Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I really do not wish to interrupt, but the implication of my learned friend from the Prosecution is that this document shows that there were soldiers ready for action is simply not correct. The witness has explained that these were military conscripts from the village of Nadioci. This is not a document indicating people ready for action, and I don't think that is proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, it's a matter for the witness to answer the question. The question which was asked is, is the position that there were soldiers on the 14th of April ready for action in Nadioci. It's for the witness to answer the question. No doubt he will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have an answer to that question, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, there were no such soldiers for any kind of action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I simply observe -- I'll deal with that later, but I will mention it just when the witness is finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's come, then, very briefly to the night of the 15th, 16th. Your function as a communications officer within your company was, and I don't mean this in any sense offensively, sufficiently low in rank that it would be quite possible for the Viteska Brigade or parts of the Viteska Brigade to be operational without your being called upon, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: It is possible, but I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know one way or another whether other parts of the Viteska Brigade were operational on the night of the 15th, 16th, given that you simply got up and went up the hill to see the fighting from a distance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were operational.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know anything about orders given at 1.00 in the morning or about compositions of troops, if there were any, at 5.30 in the morning, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you telling us that when you returned on the 15th, you were wholly unaware of any buildup of soldiers at the bungalow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me that I didn't notice anything returning from work, didn't notice any troops or any reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I missed it. When was it you returned from work that previous evening, the 15th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: On the 15th, it was in the evening. It was at the end of my regular working hours when I returned home after 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And you noticed nothing unusual in Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: On the way between there and Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice anything unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have a couple of questions, Mr. Jukic. A subject was touched upon regarding the so-called Motorolas, and I would like us to fully clarify this point. Is it correct that the name Motorola was used among the people colloquially to refer to all kinds of mobile radio transmitters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I tried to explain, but I think I didn't manage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As a professional, you know that Motorola is an American company manufacturing radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and very good-quality equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you said that you didn't notice in your battalion anyone having such a radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I would have noticed if anyone had one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were certain mobile radio transmitters?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had my own private one, a Kenwood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that such privately-owned amateur radio equipment have a limited range?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us specifically regarding your own Kenwood radio transmitter, what was its range?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Roughly three to three and a half kilometres, if the visibility was good, optical visibility. Its strength was very limited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the configuration of the terrain, hills and valleys, limit the range of radio stations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Indeed, they do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Jukic, you said that the 1st Battalion was headquartered in the building of the Workers' Education Centre in Vitez. Can you tell us with precision until when it was based there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Until the 15th of April, 1993. After that, I didn't know. I learnt later that the 1st Battalion was moved to the railway station at Impregnacija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when other battalions were formed within the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jukic, by occupation, you are a signalsman and you maintain communications equipment in a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, is communication equipment important for the effective functioning of a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I have to correct you, we didn't have any equipment. We just had-old fashioned telephones, amateur radio transmitters, a couple only, so we can't really talk about communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You've already told us that. In your opinion and on the basis of your own experience, is it necessary before any military operation to pay special attention to the functioning of communications lines?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think in all armies of the world, that is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior, immediately prior to the outbreak of the conflict in Vitez on the 16th of April, did anyone from the command of your battalion or brigade require special inspection of communications equipment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JUKIC
utterances.text: No, no one did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jukic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jukic. That concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: THE COURT: Mr. Nice, very rapidly, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to say, I'm exploring this document cautiously in the way I am, that's 653, because it does, in fact, feature in the Blaskic judgement. Therefore, the question of judicially decided facts may or may not arise. I'm proceeding cautiously, and there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now, half past nine tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday the 3rd day of August, 2000, at 9.30 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
